title: AI Is Already Better at Coding Than Most Software Developers
why_read: A personal opinion essay on AI's role in coding versus the human-centered aspects of software engineering, offering only anecdote rather than data or technical rigor.
analysis: This is a reflective, first-person piece arguing that coding itself was never the hardest or most valuable part of software engineering, and that as the author grew senior, their work shifted toward architecture, communication, and decision-making rather than raw code output. It doesn't provide any concrete technical benchmarks or evidence comparing AI coding capability to human developers despite the title's strong claim. It reads more as career reflection than as a substantiated technical argument, which limits its value for engineers seeking rigorous analysis of AI coding capability.
